examples.title: Console
examples.description: Read values from the keyboard and print text in the program console.
examples.notes: Enter a name, an age, and a height when the console asks. The IDE Diagnostics pane is not the program console.

examples.title: Comments
examples.description: Use comments to leave notes, explain intent, and temporarily disable a line while experimenting.
examples.notes: Prefer comments that explain intent or reasons instead of repeating what the code already says.

examples.title: Random Numbers
examples.description: Generate random integers and real numbers with clear ranges.
examples.notes: RandomInt includes both endpoints. RandomReal includes the minimum and excludes the maximum.

examples.title: String
examples.description: Create, index, join, and compare text values.
examples.notes: Output appears in the console. Edit the words in a Try copy and compare the results. This example uses ASCII text.

examples.title: Array
examples.description: Store several values, change elements, and copy an entire array.
examples.notes: Notice how a = b replaces the whole array, including its length. Output appears in the console.

examples.title: File
examples.description: Write and read text files, then save numbers using native binary representation.
examples.notes: Creates or overwrites example.txt, numbers.txt, and save.dat. Built-in examples run in a temporary folder. Use Try and save the copy in your own folder to keep these files.

examples.title: Window
examples.description: Set a title before opening a window, change it while open, and close the window.
examples.notes: Watch the title change after one second. The window closes automatically; the console reports its properties.

examples.title: Drawing
examples.description: A gallery of pixels, lines, rectangles, circles, colors, and text.
examples.notes: Close the graphics window when finished. Draw calls change the back buffer; Show presents the completed frame.

examples.title: Keyboard
examples.description: Compare a held key with a key that was just pressed or released.
examples.notes: Click the graphics window, then try the arrow keys, Space, Enter, Escape, Tab, Backspace, Delete, and A/B/C. Messages appear in the console.

examples.title: Mouse
examples.description: Track the mouse position and the state of three mouse buttons.
examples.notes: Move inside the graphics window. Left press, right release, and holding the middle button print messages to the console.

examples.title: StopWatch
examples.description: Measure elapsed time and reset the reference point.
examples.notes: Runs automatically. Elapsed time is in seconds; the printed values can be a little longer than the requested sleeps.

examples.title: Timer
examples.description: Call a named function repeatedly without calling it from the loop yourself.
examples.notes: Prints ticks for about three seconds, then stops. Sleep lets the Small event loop deliver timer callbacks.

examples.title: Sound
examples.description: Play every sound preset and compare immediate playback with waiting.
examples.notes: Audio plays automatically. Functions ending in AndWait wait for that sound; the other functions return immediately.

examples.title: C++ Interop
examples.description: Use the C++ standard library alongside Small, with explicit Small:: names.
examples.notes: Advanced bridge example. The Small IDE still supplies the runtime and calls SmallMain; this is not a stand-alone main() project.

examples.title: ASCII Art
examples.description: Draw an X inside a square using nested loops and text output.
examples.notes: Enter a small positive size, such as 12. Try changing the characters or the drawing condition.

examples.title: Number Guessing
examples.description: Guess a secret number using higher/lower clues and count your attempts.
examples.notes: Each run chooses a new secret number from 1 to 100.

examples.title: Drawing Pad
examples.description: Draw and erase on a canvas with the mouse.
examples.notes: Left button: blue brush. Right button: eraser. Space: clear. The canvas is not cleared every frame, so the marks remain.

examples.title: Bouncing Ball
examples.description: Animate a ball that bounces against the edges and makes a sound on impact.
examples.notes: Runs automatically. Try changing the speed, radius, color, or window size.

examples.title: Reaction Timer
examples.description: Wait for a timer signal, then measure the time until you press Enter.
examples.notes: Use the console: press Enter to begin, wait for the beep, then press Enter again. A simple timing demonstration, not a calibrated reaction-time test.

examples.title: Pong
examples.description: A one-player paddle game: keep the ball from escaping past the left edge.
examples.notes: Click the graphics window. Up/Down move the paddle. Missing the ball resets it. Close the window or use Stop to finish.

examples.title: Save Game
examples.description: Save game values to a binary file and load them back.
examples.notes: Enter a level, score, and play time. Creates or overwrites save.dat using native int/double bytes. Save a Try copy in your own folder to keep the file.
